sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for opportunity tables
sections.what: Brings in the column types and the SQL helper needed to define the opportunity tables.
sections.why: These tables cannot be defined without these imports.

sections.name: opportunitySettings
sections.title: Opportunity scanner settings
sections.what: Holds the settings for the opportunity scanner: whether it is enabled, which industries it covers, how often it runs in hours, stored fingerprints, and when it last swept.
sections.why: Likely reason: one settings row controls the scheduled sweeps. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprints field is a free key and value map, and its meaning is not stated in the code.

sections.name: opportunityJobs
sections.title: Queue of opportunity sweep jobs
sections.what: Holds one row per sweep job, with its industry, trigger, status, counts of sources checked and signals found, coverage notes, any error, and start and finish times. Only one queued or running job is allowed per industry.
sections.why: The unique active index stops two sweeps for the same industry from overlapping. The queue index supports ordered processing.
sections.watch_out: A job left in queued or running blocks any new sweep for that industry until it is cleared.

sections.name: opportunitySignals
sections.title: Opportunity signals found
sections.what: Stores each possible opportunity found for an industry, with its payload, review status (new by default), and the first and last times it was seen.
sections.why: Likely reason: the review status supports a person deciding what to do with each signal. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: The payload has no fixed shape in the database, so bad data will not be rejected here.

sections.name: researchSources
sections.title: Research sources table
sections.what: Stores research source records as a flexible payload with a set of source keys.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The table has no timestamps or indexes, which suggests it is a simple lookup store.
sections.watch_out: Its purpose is not explained in the code, so confirm with the code that writes it before changing it.

summary: Defines four tables for the opportunity scanner: settings, sweep jobs, found signals, and a research sources table.
purpose: Stores what the opportunity scanner runs on, what it has queued, and what it has found.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The table and field names suggest a scheduled scan of industries for signals.
how: It imports the column types it needs. Then it defines the settings table, the job queue, the signal list, and the sources table, each with its columns and indexes.
inputs: Not visible in this file. Rows are written by code elsewhere.
outputs: Table definitions and the column structure used by the rest of the app.
risks: Several payload fields are untyped JSON, so the database does not check their shape. The job table has a rule that blocks a second active job for the same industry.
debug: If a new sweep will not start for an industry, check whether an existing job is still in queued or running state for that industry. If settings seem ignored, check the enabled flag and the interval in hours.
